newsitem.title: USA: Triple Crown seen adding $13 mln to NYC economy.
newsitem.headline: Triple Crown seen adding $13 mln to NYC economy.

text.p: The appearance of Triple Crown contender Silver Charm in the Belmont Stakes will almost double the economic impact on New York City to $13 million, Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said Wednesday.

The horse race, to be held on June 7, normally generates about $7.7 million in spending, he said. But for the first time since 1989, a horse is entering the race with the chance to win the third leg of the Triple Crown.

Silver Charm previously won the Kentucky Derby and the Preakness, the first two legs of the Triple Crown. Only 23 horses have entered the Belmont Stakes with a shot at the Triple Crown. Saturday will market the 129th running.
"New York City has never been accused of being a one-horse town, but this week we don't mind the designation one bit," the mayor said.

Giuliani said one-third of Belmont Park is located in New York City, with the remainder in Elmont, N.Y., in suburban Nassau County. Tax revenues are split accordingly, he said, with the city expecting $500,000 from this year's Belmont Stakes, up from $300,000.
"The horses actually race across county lines," Giuliani said, adding that he likes to consider it a New York City event.
